extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, geometers, or advanced students studying classical constructions of conic sections and trajectory problems (Newton/Apollonius-style geometry)
extracted.subtask_description: Geometric constructions and criteria for describing conic sections (ellipses, parabolas, hyperbolas) and orbital trajectories from given data: foci (umbilici), vertices, latus rectum, given points and/or tangents. Includes lemmas giving tangency criteria, and procedures to find missing foci or construct the conic from various combinations of given elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 1 (from previous proposition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the principal vertex D, the latus rectum L, and one focus (umbilicus) S of a conic section, the other focus H is determined by taking DH to DS as latus rectum to the difference between the latus rectum and 4×DS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proportion used: SP + PH to PH as 2SP to L; in this corollary DS + DH to DH is 4DS to L, and dividing gives DS to DH as (4DS - L) to L. Use that relation to locate H (both length and position).

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the velocity of the body at the principal vertex D, the orbit (conic) can be found quickly by taking the latus rectum proportional to twice the distance DS in the duplicate ratio of the given velocity to the velocity of a body moving in a circle at distance DS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (Refers to Coroll. 3 of Theor. VIII.) Then DH to DS is as latus rectum to the difference between latus rectum and 4DS. Practical rule for constructing orbit from vertex data and speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 3
rubrics_metrics.description: If a body moves in any conic section and receives any impulse from its orbit, the subsequent orbit can be determined by composing the body's original motion with the motion that the impulse alone would generate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretative principle: combine the proper motion of the body with the motion produced by the impulse to obtain the new motion and thus the new orbit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary 4
rubrics_metrics.description: If a body is continuously perturbed by an external force, the course may be approximated by collecting the discrete changes at certain points and estimating the continuous mutation by analogy of the series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Method of successive approximations: observe induced changes at sample points, infer continuous changes in intermediate locations, and thereby estimate the perturbed path.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XV (tangency criterion from two foci)
rubrics_metrics.description: If from two foci (umbilici) S, H of an ellipse or hyperbola two lines SV and HV are drawn to any third point V such that one (HV) equals the transverse axis and the other (SV) is bisected by a perpendicular TR dropped from V, then the perpendicular TR touches the conic; conversely, if TR touches the conic then VH equals the axis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric test for tangency using equal segments and angle-bisection: check equality of HV to transverse axis and bisected SV by perpendicular to infer contact (or infer equality of VH from tangency). Useful as a local tangency criterion in constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XVIII (Prob. X): construct ellipse or hyperbola from given focus, transverse axis length, a point and a tangent
rubrics_metrics.description: Given common focus S, transverse axis length AB, a point P which the trajectory must pass through, and a line TR which it must be tangent to, construct the ellipse (or hyperbola) through P tangent to TR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction steps: if orbit is ellipse take circle center P radius AB - SP (or AB + SP for hyperbola); drop perpendicular ST from S to tangent TR and extend to V so that TV = ST; with center V and radius AB draw another circle; the common intersection H of the two circles gives the second focus; then with foci S,H and major axis SP+PH (ellipse) or SP-PH (hyperbola) the conic is determined. The proof appeals to the defining sum/difference equalities of conics and Lemma XV for tangency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XIX (Prob. XI): construct parabola from given focus, point(s), or tangent(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given focus S, a point P through which the parabolic trajectory must pass, and a tangent TR which it must touch, construct the parabola.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: with center P draw circle FG radius PS; drop perpendicular ST from S to TR and extend to V so TV = ST; similarly for another given point or tangent; draw common tangent IF to the two circles (or determine intersection constructs depending on which data are given); drop perpendicular SI to IF, bisect it in K, and describe the parabola with vertex K and axis SK. Justification uses equalities SK=IK and SP=FP and previous lemmas (esp. Lemma XIV Cor.3) for tangency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XX (Prob. XII): construct conic of given species through points or tangent conditions (cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a focus S and that the conic is of a given species (ellipse, parabola, hyperbola), construct the trajectory passing through two given points, or tangent to two given lines, or passing through a point and tangent to a line — several cases addressed with constructions that yield the needed conic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case 1 (two given points): use the given ratio of transverse axis to focus distance to choose points K, L on SP and SP (or analogous) and draw circles centered at the given points; use common tangent to these circles to get intersection A and a corresponding axis; with axes at vertices A and a describe the conic. Case 2 (two tangents): drop perpendiculars from S to the tangents, extend to points V,v with TV=TS, etc; bisect Vv, erect perpendicular OH, and find intersections K,k to determine VH etc; then construct conic with foci S,H. Case 3 (given point and tangent): similar reduction to case 2 by constructing auxiliary parallels and circles. Case 4 (complex combination of point/tangent similar to earlier cases): use proportional constructions and similarity of triangles to show the constructed conic passes through the given data and has the appropriate axis-to-focus distance ratio. The general guidance: reduce to constructions of circles and use symmetry/similarity and Lemma XV for tangency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XVI (construct fourth point given three and linear-difference constraints)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given three points A,B,C and a fourth unknown point Z where the differences (or zeros) of lengths AZ, BZ, CZ satisfy given relations, Z can be located via intersections of appropriate hyperbolae or special loci.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case 1: If difference between AZ and BZ is given, locate Z on hyperbola with foci A,B having that transverse axis (axis MN). Use proportional constructions involving perpendiculars/normals to locate Z by intersection of lines from constructions on three hyperbolae (one for each pair) to get Z as intersection. Case 2: If two lengths equal, Z lies on perpendicular bisector; Case 3: If all three equal, Z is the circumcenter. References Vieta/Apollonius restoration. Useful to solve constrained-locus problems by intersecting standard conic loci.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXI (Prob. XIII): find the other focus given one focus, a point and a tangent
rubrics_metrics.description: Given focus S, point P, and tangent TR on the desired trajectory, find the other focus H and thereby the conic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drop perpendicular ST to tangent TR and extend it to Y so that TY = ST; then YH equals the transverse axis. Join SP and HP; SP equals the difference between HP and the transverse axis. Repeating for additional given points or tangents yields lines YH or PH whose ratios or differences either equal axes or differ by given lengths; then apply the earlier lemma to find H. Once foci and axis length are known (YH or PH+SP etc.), construct the conic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholium (fast solution when three points are given)
rubrics_metrics.description: When three points B,C,D on the conic are given, a faster construction finds the vertex and axis by proportional constructions from extensions of BC and CD and drawing normals and parallels, yielding the vertex A and axis Aa from which the conic type (ellipse/parabola/hyperbola) is determined by the relative size of GA to AS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: extend BC and CD to E,F so EB:EC = SB:SC and FC:FD = SC:SD; on EF draw normals and construct GA proportional to AS as described; then A is the vertex and Aa the transverse axis. Evaluate GA relative to AS to determine conic species. Also references De la Hire for similar methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XVII (ratio property for lines from a point to sides of a trapezoid)
rubrics_metrics.description: If from a point P inside (or related to) a trapezoid ABCD four lines PQ, PR, PS, PT are drawn to the four sides at given equal angles, then the rectangle PQ×PR is to rectangle PS×PT in a given ratio (determined by the trapezoid geometry).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof covers three cases: (1) when opposite sides are parallel; (2) when not parallel and parallels are constructed to reduce; (3) general inclination. The lemma gives a proportionality relation between the products of pairs of intercepts cut off on sides and is foundational for later tangency/inscribed-conic criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XVIII (converse: rectangle ratio implies tangency)
rubrics_metrics.description: With the same setup as Lemma XVII, if the rectangle PQ×PR is in the given ratio to PS×PT, then the point P from which the four lines are drawn lies on the conic section inscribed about the trapezoid (i.e., P is a tangency point).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by assuming a conic through the four trapezoid vertices and a generic point p on it and transferring the rectangle ratio via Lemma XVII to the given PQ×PR:PS×PT equality; contradiction if P is not on the conic implies P must be on the conic. This gives a construction/test: check product ratios to determine tangency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary to Lemma XVIII (three-line condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: If three lines PQ, PR, PS from a common point P to three given lines AB, CD, AC are such that PQ×PR to PS^2 is in a given ratio, then P lies on the conic that is tangent to AB and CD at the corresponding contact points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a specialized application: set the trapezoid with two equal lines and apply the lemma; it yields a practical condition for locating P on a conic tangent to two given lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XIX (construct the point P from four given position lines with prescribed rectangle ratio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given four position lines (that is, four fixed lines in given positions) AB, CD, AC, BD and the condition that if from point P four lines PQ, PR, PS, PT are drawn to these lines respectively then PQ×PR : PS×PT has a specified ratio, there is a method to find P.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: take any line AH in which P is to be sought; intersect AH with opposite lines to get H,I; using given angular data and known ratios deduce PQ:PS, then subtract that from the prescribed PQ×PR:PS×PT to obtain PR:PT; adding known ratios PI:PR and PT:PH gives PI:PH and thus fixes P. Corollaries: tangents through arbitrary locus points and global locus construction (parabola/ellipse/hyperbola) follow by varying the auxiliary choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XX (parallelogram tangent-to-conic abscissa ratio)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a parallelogram ASPQ with opposite angles A and P tangent to a conic at A and P has its sides continued infinitely so that intersections with the conic occur, then the abscissae parts PR and PT (intercepts on one side) are in a given ratio; conversely if those abscissae parts have the given ratio, the constructed point D will be a tangency point for the conic through the four intersection points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction and converse: use parallels and similar triangles and apply Lemma XVII-style rectangle ratios to derive PR:PT. The converse proceeds by reversing the proportional equalities to show tangency (via Lemma XVIII). Corollaries give methods to obtain tangents at known points and to relate tangency conditions and ratios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XXI (moving poles/lines produce conic as envelope)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two variable lines BM, CM through fixed poles B, C have their intersection M run along a given line MN, and other two variable lines BD, CD making fixed angles with the first pair intersect at D, then the locus of D is a conic section through B and C; conversely, if D runs on a conic through B,C,A then the corresponding M will move on the given fixed line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses similarity of triangles and proportional relations PT:PR to NM, then Lemma XX to show D traces a conic. This lemma gives a dynamic construction viewpoint: generating a conic as the envelope/locus of intersection points of varying lines constrained by fixed poles/angles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXII (Prob. XIV): construct conic through five given points
rubrics_metrics.description: Given five distinct points A,B,C,D,P, construct the conic passing through them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction: choose two of the points as poles B,C and rotate corresponding lines through given angles to produce pairs of lines TPS, PRQ through a fourth point; extend and consider intersections T,R, take proportional small segments Pt,Pr on PT,PR and let the lines from their poles meet at d; in the limiting process as those auxiliary segments tend to zero (or via the finite construction), the intersection point d tends to D and the locus gives the conic through the five points. Alternative equivalent mechanical construction via rotating limbs about poles is described. Corollaries: tangents, centers, diameters and latus rectum can be found by related constructions (see Lem. XIX).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXIII (Prob. XV): construct conic through four points and tangent at one (two cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a tangent HB with contact B and three other points C,D,P, construct the conic through the four points and tangent at B. Two constructive approaches are given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case 1: form parallelogram BSPQ with PQ∥BC, PS∥BH, find intersections and proportional abscissae Pr,Pt on PR,PT proportional to chosen segments, then intersections of corresponding constructed lines give the conic points (use Lem. XX). Alternative: rotate given angle CBH about B and roll a radius about C to record intersection points M,N and trace the locus of their envelope; intersection of moving radius with the rotated limb delineates the conic. Case 2: if the remaining four points lie off the tangent, intersection of certain constructed lines and use of mean proportionals yields the contact point A; then proceed as in Case 1. Both methods rely on prior lemmas (XVII-XX) and similarity/proportion relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXIV (Prob. XVI): construct conic through three points and two given tangents
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two tangents HI, KL and three points B,C,D (or their intersections with tangents), construct the conic passing through the three points and tangent to the two lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct BD and CD intersecting tangents at known points; find points R,S by cutting RS so that HR:KR equals the mean proportional of BH:HD to BK:KD etc., and IS:LS equals analogous mean proportional for C; the secant RS meets the tangent lines at contact points A and P which are tangency points; with those contact points the conic is constructed as in previous problems. Use the property that IZ (mean proportional) squared relates to rectangles formed by intersection points per conic properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma XXII (transforming figures into others of same genus)
rubrics_metrics.description: A general method to transform a figure into another of the same genus (same analytic order) via affine-like mappings preserving ratios: use two given parallels AO, BL and a third line AB as a reference; map points by parallels and proportional parallels about chosen centers; tangency, order (degree) and other incidence/tangency properties are preserved under the mapping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed mapping: given a point G on the original figure, construct a corresponding g by drawing GD parallel to OA, and then producing OD to meet BL, then erecting gd at given angle and proportional to GD:OD to give gd:OD. The lemma proves that if G is tangent to a given line or conic, so is g to the corresponding transformed line/curve. It also asserts preservation of analytic order (line→line, conic→conic, cubic→cubic etc.). This is a tool to simplify constructions by transforming difficult configurations to simpler ones (e.g., make converging lines parallel) and inverting the transformation to recover the solution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prop. XXV (Prob. XVII): construct conic through two points and three tangents
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two points and three tangents (lines that the conic must touch), construct the conic. The method reduces the figure by a transformation (Lemma XXII) to a simpler configuration where two tangents are parallel and the third is parallel to the line joining the two given points, solve there, and inverse-transform the contact points back to the original configuration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the transformed figure take parallelogram of the three tangents and a line through the two points; determine contact points c,d,e in the transformed figure using proportional constructions relating distances from sides to squares of rectangles as per conic properties; then inverse-transform these contact points into the original figure and proceed with constructions from Problem XIV to obtain the conic. The proposition gives explicit relations for proportioning hc, ic, ke, el to sides and rectangles to ensure constructed contacts are correct.
